title: Singapore Travel Thread
body:
O.P.
I saw Scoot have one way flights to Singapore advertised at only $123! Wow. So now I'm interested about going.
How long would be a good length of time? I'm thinking a week.
Is English spoken and written fairly widely?
The things I've found so far that I want to do are...
- Singapore Zoo - Gardens by the Bay dome world things - Chinatown - Sentosa - Marina Bay - Clarkes Quay - Singapore Flier - Maybe Underwater World (is it any better than Seaworld on the Gold Coast?) - National museum - Orchard Road
I think a week would be a heap of time to do those things at a leisurely pace.
I've heard the big chain hotels are bland and overpriced. What hotels have people here liked in their visits?
I am tossing up between staying at Clarkes Quay, Marina Bay or the general downtown area (whatever that is...not quite sure). I know public transport is excellent there. I want to be staying in a place with a similar vibe to say, Circular Quay in Sydney. I want to walk out my hotel foyer door and be amongst it. Lots of people, vibrancy, lights, an alive vibe, very busy and lit up at night with heaps of restaurants (not so much bars or clubs though) and shops.
What kind of food is around? This may sound stupid, but is it all Asian varieties? Chinese, Japanese, Thai, Malaysian, Korean, etc? Or do they also have Italian, Indian, and US / Australian style fusion type things we have here?
What are the better months to go in terms of weather? Is it very hot there usually? I don't mind some heat, but I'd prefer to go at a time when it's comfortable to wander around in the day and night.
I think that's it. For now. HEH.
Thank you!

---- replies ----
[User #3102044452 poststubby74Whirlpool Forums Addict] graceslick writes...
What are the better months to go in terms of weather? Is it very hot there usually? I don't mind some heat, but I'd prefer to go at a time when it's comfortable to wander around in the day and night.
I believe you will find 10 months of the year it's 32C and 99% humidity, 2 months of the year it's 31C. there's no avoiding it. there's plenty of Italian, little india has a huge selection from all over india. western food can be had if you want but if you're after a big steak it wont be cheap. for the zoo, daytime is ok but the night safari is what you really want. Right next door is the river safari, also worth a visit. there's plenty of life on orchard road every night of the week with shops open and well visited to 10pm each night. Stayed there with the family about a year ago and the only thing is nothing much is open until 10 or 11am either. Clarke/boat quay areas are probably better for the lively area you want.

[User #33417012832 postsagielWhirlpool Forums Addict] this post was edited
graceslick writes...
How long would be a good length of time? I'm thinking a week.
one week is ok...i believe for my first time visit i had stayed 12 days and i could of stayed longer! (which i ended up a year later doing lol) so i've pretty much done all the tourist attractions and nature parks/reserves and visited most parts of Singapore.
yes everyone knows English no issue, get used to the accent ok la lol
go S.E.A Aquarium it is much better than Underwater world
the zoo (day and night) will take a whole day Gardens by the Bay takes a few hours, maybe 2 or 3 Chinatown/Little India/Arab street/Clarke Quay you can do that in a day (depending if you go to the museums and temples or just walk around)
Sentosa (mmm 2 days here if you want to do everything, especially if you want to go SEA aquarium) and add another day if you want to do Adventure Cove WaterPark Universal Studios (if you want to do everything will take a day, as in morning until 5) Marina Bay can just walk around before or after you do Gardens by the Bay
Singapore Flier can do at night or day, doesn't take too long
National Museum a few hours i guess the Peranakan museum is quite interesting too and the ArtScience Museum and the Art Museum
Orchard Road this can be done at any time just a whole lot of shopping malls. If you want a lot of exercise you could walk this whole road all the way up to the Botanical Gardens and then take the train and maybe eat at Holland Village.
I've heard the big chain hotels are bland and overpriced. What hotels have people here liked in their visits?
hotels in Singapore are not cheap!
i've personally stayed at Victoria Hotel in the Downtown Core area (first hotel i ever stayed at when i first visited Singapore) i enjoyed it, small but clean, comfortable, had computers in the reception area for guests to use. V Hotel Lavender Marina Bay Sands resort Swissotel at Stamford hotel Regin Hotel in Geyland area Orchard Parade hotel Bay Hotel (opposite VivoCity) i've also had a look inside Green Kiwi Backpacker Hostel and i've stayed at some place in the Tanjong Pagar district which i can't remember the name of and i've also stayed in the Pasir Ris area, Ang Mo Kio area and Bendemeer area, but these are like suburbs which you probably don't want to stay for your first visit!
yea i would stay there too...Clarke Quay area, Bugis, Lavender, Chinatown, City Hall...around this area...although if you are close to an MRT station then you won't have any issues. Little India if you like Indian food!
similar vibe...yea Clarke Quay the lively area. Chinatown is also happening but not along the riverside! yea Clarke Quay has a lot of restaurants along the river too and has clubs and bars lol
if you want cheap food you stick to the hawker centres. THey have western in the hawker centres too but the food quality mmm is ok (can get the western food for $7-10)...you go more for the asian food. chinese, malay, indian
if you want like western food go to astons (love this place for the cheap western food) i like hot tomato too for cheap western. when i say cheap i mean like $15 for a steak or something.
if you want something better than you got to pay for it!
It's always hot! But like end of November, December, Jan is more rainy but that's why you can reach a lot of places by simply walking through the malls in the aircon...the trains and buses are also fine
august and september is good because it's their national day and the mid autumn festival so they will have lot's of decorations up

[User #4678306193 postsDuNnoWhirlpool Forums Addict] graceslick writes...
What kind of food is around? This may sound stupid, but is it all Asian varieties?
It's very multi-cultural in Singapore due to it being a business hub. You can find anything/everything ranging from food court food to top tier restaurants. There's anything/everything from hawker Asian food to Italian to fast food.
[User #62076260 postsushererParticipant] hey there, Singaporean here.
Some alternative suggestions here :)
Accommodation: Both of these are pretty swanky hostels that still come in cheaper than hotels. They're smack in the middle of Chinatown (don't worry about staying there. SG has the cleanest Chinatown in the world (which also means, not very authentic...)) www.adlerhostel.com www.5footwayinn.com/ – This has several locations, all of which are in areas that have the vibe you are looking for.
Places to visit: If you are willing to return with snapshots that are different from other tourists, check out these, or at least some of them: Haw Par Villa Katong area, with its Peranakan shophouses Bukit Brown cemetary – gorgeous Chinese tombstones Arab Street/Kampong Glam area – to smoke shisha (before it's banned)
The language of instruction and business is English, so getting around is of no problem.
A number of Singaporeans speak a form of pidgin English, known as Singlish. But you would be understood and you should be able to understand perfectly fine. Do note that 40% of the people around you would be foreigners – mainland Chinese, Vietnamese, Burmese, Bengali – so there is still a good chance you may not get an English speaker the first time you approach someone.
You might note this being the case, it's actually quite a hassle for older Singaporeans who do not speak English, and they're actually quite disenfranchised and vulnerable. Such is the state of affairs in the country.
On the brighter note, for tourists, Singapore is an English-speaking smorgaboard of everything from all over the world, engineered for tourism purposes.
[User #1896253333 postsgraceslickWhirlpool Forums Addict] O.P.
Oh wow! I feel bad for the older Singapore people being vulnerable and isolated for not speaking a FOREIGN language in their own country! :(
I'm more excited than ever about going there now, after reading all this stuff!!!
I actually love Asian food so wouldn't have a problem if it was all Asian, but I may have a hankering for a burger or for pasta or pizza, which is why I asked.
Singlish is fine. Anything is fine really. I would never expect to be understood by most people in a non-English as first language country. I would find that a bit arrogant. I'd just be happy to be understood on a basic level by people in restaurants and who I need to talk to in order to get around ok. :)

[User #9498841351 postsSirFlibblenow in 4KWhirlpool Forums Addict] Last time I was in Singapore I stayed at the Royal Hotel on Scott. Right by Orchard Road. Paid about $180 a night including all you can eat mini-bar.
Singapore has literally every type of food, but if you take the train out a few stations, get off and walk down any road, you'll end find a hawker centre. More authentic singaporean food then you find in the touristy areas and will cost about $3-4 for a meal.
Keep an eye out for Chilli Crab, Behoon, fried carrot cake, chicken rice and BBQ Singray.
